title: The eye sign
logline: A hand-painted sign with an eye on it in a shop window on main street, new this summer, unexplained. The strip would have made a joke. The page draws it straight and moves on.

panels.composition: Main street, late August, the light going long. A storefront that was Wagner's Hardware, then empty, then something else: in its window, a hand-painted sign — a single open eye, no words — propped against the glass. The reflection of the street in the window over it. The seawall at the far end. The ridge glow above the roofs, large.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a small-town main street in long late-August light with a former hardware storefront whose window holds a hand-painted sign of a single open eye with no words propped against the glass, the street reflected over it, a seawall at the far end, a large warm glow above the rooftops, no people, no words
image.notes: Vol 7's sign. Draw it plain. No joke.
